text:
kevin: Heads up — noticing a spike in streaming stalls for /v1/generate on rwd-medium-8q since last night. Token tail latency ~3x, clients report pauses mid-stream. I dumped a profiler and low-level traces.

maria: saw the alert. did we push a kernel change or batching tweak yesterday? @kevin

kevin: yes, kernel-selector v2.1 rolled at 02:10 UTC (int8 fast paths). also bump to batching window 4ms by default. perf-bot uploaded flamegraphs: https://perf.internal/fg/1712345600

perf-bot: Profile summary (rooted at request):
- total token latency (median): 12ms/token -> bulk of increase in tail
- kv_fetch median: 28ms (was 6ms pre-rollout)
- stream_send gaps: frequent 80-300ms gaps at chunk boundaries
- enqueue/batching overhead: +3ms median

liam: matching signal from Dedicated west. per-route KPIs for /v1/generate: p95 went from 420ms -> 1.3s after the roll; error budget burn increasing. Looks correlated with requests that hit prefix KV cache misses.

sarah: can we add token-level latency breakdowns to the console dashboard? need per-route token breakdown (compute, kv, serialization, network) and client vs server timing so customers see where stalls occur.

kevin: quick hypothesis: kernel selector picks int8 kernel that alters memory layout -> increases KV lookup cost because cache hits are now misaligned to page boundaries. Also batching window 4ms may be causing mid-chunk flushes for streaming cadence.

maria: quick repro idea: run same prompt on v2.0 kernel vs v2.1 with identical batcher config and KV cache warmed vs cold, measure chunk cadence. I'll spin up canary jobs.

ops-bot: Collected traces for sample request 1712345723: trace link https://traces.internal/trace/1712345723, logs: https://logs.internal/q?id=1712345723

kevin: small config snippet I'm testing locally (will push to canary):
```
kernel_selector:
  strategy: prefer_stable
  fallback: latest
batcher:
  window_ms: 8
  max_tokens: 256
kv_cache:
  prefix_cache: true
  page_align: true
```

liam: try with prefix_cache=false too — if misalignment is the issue disabling prefix cache should reduce the kv_fetch spike.

perf-bot: quick numbers from a short run (1000 requests, 64 token prompts):
- v2.0 + window 4ms: median token 10ms, kv_fetch 6ms, stream_gap ~30ms
- v2.1 + window 4ms: median token 13ms, kv_fetch 28ms, stream_gap 120ms
- v2.1 + window 8ms: median token 12ms, kv_fetch 22ms, stream_gap 60ms

sarah: action items for dashboards:
- add a token-latency heatmap per-route (bucket by token index)
- show kv_fetch vs compute per-token stacked bars
- surface stream chunk cadence (ms between chunk sends) and % of streams with >100ms gap

kevin: short plan:
1) rollback kernel-selector to v2.0 for prod regions A/B this morning (canary already running v2.1)
2) run A/B with batching window 4ms vs 8ms and prefix_cache on/off
3) add token-level metrics to the console and alert on stream_gap p95 > 150ms
Assignees: maria (canary runs + rollback), liam (per-route KPIs + dashboards), sarah (dashboard panels), kevin (root cause and kernel follow-up)

maria: starting rollback now for region-a, patch ETA 20m. will post when live.

kevin: thanks — also let's add a short smoke test that asserts consistent chunk cadence <50ms variance for 90% of tokens before promoting new kernel. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: posted perf regression ticket: PERF-8723, linked to traces and flamegraphs.

ops-bot: rollback to v2.0 in region-a completed at 1712345830 UTC. monitoring now.

liam: region-a numbers look back to baseline — p95 down to 430ms. leaving canary alone until we validate kv/cache alignment changes.

sarah: I'll prototype the token heatmap panel and post the query in #eng-infra once ready.

kevin: great work team, keep updates in this thread. if anyone sees a new stall after rollback ping here.
